player.seasonOutlook: Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance in a Los Angeles tight end room that also includes ascending Oronde Gadsden II. Njoku will only be worth a late flier if he quickly takes control as the team's clear starter at the position.

Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

Johnson's rookie season didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start under new coach Mike McCarthy, but he still has a steep hill to climb with Warren and newcomer Rico Dowdle ahead of him on depth chart. He's only worth rostering in dynasty.

Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with Emmett Johnson and Emari Demercado for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

Tonges enters his fourth NFL season very much on the fantasy radar due to a torn Achilles suffered by George Kittle during last season's playoffs. Kittle is expected to return at some point this season, but while he's out, Tonges is set to replace him as the 49ers' top pass catcher at the position. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson. Tonges will be a fringe TE1 as long as Kittle is sidelined and is thus worth late-round consideration.

Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising �breakout� players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Stowers was selected by the Eagles in the second round of April's draft. Stowers is a converted quarterback who improved his production each of the last three seasons, peaking with a 62-769-4 receiving line in 2025. He aligned in the slot on 72% of his collegiate routes (highest among this rookie tight end class) and his career 2.38 YPRR is easily tops in this TE class. He's not much of a blocker, but he sports good speed and athleticism (he posted the best vertical and broad jumps among TEs at the combine). Stowers will have minimal fantasy value while working behind Dallas Goedert as a rookie, but he has long-term TE1 upside and will be a popular breakout candidate in 2027.

Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor will play a role in the New York offense, but he won't see nearly enough targets to allow any sort of fantasy relevance.

Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the fantasy radar.

Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare is nowhere close to fantasy relevance at the moment.

Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

Richardson enters his fourth NFL season currently as a backup to Daniel Jones, but still a candidate to be traded. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passing style are the only reason to keep him stashed in deep dynasty leagues.
